title: 'Big Short' Michael Burry Says OpenAI, Anthropic Want To Join Big Tech's Oligopoly — But Much Of AI Spending May Become 'Sunk Cost'
source_used: Yahoo Finance copy of a StockTwits article (the copy says 'originally published on StockTwits')
key_facts: In his latest Substack post, published on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026, Michael Burry argued that 'compression' will make some AI investments uneconomical.
Burry wrote that much of what is being spent on AI will become sunk cost, meaning money that cannot be recovered.
He said OpenAI and Anthropic want to join an oligopoly of Microsoft, Amazon, Google and Meta, but that this is a want, not a need.
Hyperscaler capital spending is expected to approach $800 billion in 2026 and could top $1 trillion in 2027.
Burry said the market could be heading for a sizable correction in the coming months.
The article lists Burry's bearish positions in Nvidia, Palantir, Oracle, Micron, Nebius, the iShares Semiconductor ETF and the Nasdaq 100.
Nvidia hit a record high on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026.
quote_evidence: Ultimately, compression will do its deed, and much of what is being spent will be just so much sunk cost.
They intend to be part of the oligopoly. None can imagine breaking the dominance of a Microsoft, Amazon, Google, or Meta within each silo.
why_it_matters_hint: A prominent investor's bearish opinion on AI spending, from a blog post, with no detail on what 'compression' means.
notes: Read on Yahoo Finance, which carries a StockTwits article ('This article was originally published on StockTwits'). Credit goes to StockTwits; the copy gives no StockTwits link, so the Yahoo link is used. Burry's Substack post was not opened. This is an opinion piece; positions are as the article reports them.
